title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 7-9): X and Y are topological surfaces of finite type, 'combinatoires' (compact surfaces minus finitely many points). The objects of study are finite étale maps (finite topological coverings) X -> Y up to isotopy. The previous page shows the following. The components of the space of finite étale maps X -> Y are contractible. The Teichmüller group T_X = A_X/A_X^0 acts on Hom_ext(X,Y) with finite stabilizers, namely the deck groups of the covering Y'_f -> Y. The orbits are in bijection with R_X(Y), the isomorphism classes of finite étale covers of Y homeomorphic to X, and this orbit set is finite.

This page first completes that statement: the orbits under T_X^+ correspond to R_X(Y) x {±1}. The sign records whether the covering map preserves or reverses orientation, giving the splitting into Hom^+_isot(X,Y) and Hom^-_isot(X,Y).

Scholie: composition of isotopy classes makes oriented surfaces of finite type, with Hom^+_isot as morphisms, into a category, the 'catégorie isotopique orientée des surfaces orientées combinatoires'. It is described as equivalent to a quotient of a category of quadruples (X, Y, Y', f_0). Here Y' -> Y is a finite étale cover and f_0 lies in Isom^+_isot(X, Y'), an oriented isotopy class of homeomorphisms. In other words, a morphism is a cover of Y together with a marking of it by X, taken up to isotopy. From here on all surfaces are oriented, all maps preserve orientation, and the + is dropped.

Formula (12) then defines the profinite completion of the Hom-sets as a contracted product: Hom^(X,Y) = Hom_isot(X,Y) ∧^{T_X} \hat T_X. Since the oriented mapping class group T_X acts with finite stabilizers H_i and finitely many orbits, Hom_isot(X,Y) = ⊔_i T_X/H_i. Then Hom^(X,Y) = ⊔_i \hat T_X / H_i, a profinite (compact) space. The marginal notes say it is 'muni de la topologie d'espace compact' and call it a 'compactifié profini'. The map Hom -> Hom^ is injective because T_X is residually finite.

Formula (13) announces a composition Hom^(X,Y) x Hom^(Y,Z) -> Hom^(X,Z). The next page adds that associativity should follow 'par continuité', remarks 'Mérite d'être fait avec plus de soin!', and turns to an axiomatics of categories with profinite automorphism groups ('Galois axiomatique').

Aim: to build a profinitely completed 'Teichmüller category' of surfaces and finite covers. It is the natural object on which Gal(\bar Q/Q) should act, compatibly with the outer actions on the \hat T_X (= \hat Γ_{g,n}, the geometric fundamental groups of the moduli stacks M_{g,n}). In this way the Galois action on the whole Teichmüller tower is made functorial with respect to finite étale covers of curves, not only with respect to the operations of degeneration and gluing.
errors: The description of the equivalent quotient category is muddled in the manuscript (several crossed-out attempts). The intended equivalence relation on quadruples (identifying Y' up to Y-isomorphism, i.e. modulo deck transformations) is not stated.

Composition (13) is only announced, not constructed. It requires a further step: for u: X -> Y, the classes in T_Y lifting along u form a finite-index subgroup, and lifting gives a homomorphism from it to T_X, defined only up to the finite deck group. This homomorphism must then be extended to profinite completions. It does extend, because any homomorphism between discrete groups is continuous for the full profinite topologies. Associativity 'by continuity/density' is plausible, but Grothendieck himself flags it as needing care.

Injectivity of Hom -> Hom^ and the identification of the completed orbits \hat T_X/H use that finite subgroups survive in \hat T_X, i.e. residual finiteness of mapping class groups (Grossman 1974). This is implicit and not stated.

ideas.what: Splitting of the orbit set of T_X^+ on Hom_ext(X,Y) into R_X(Y) x {±1} by orientation behaviour
ideas.modern_name: Orientation-preserving vs reversing covers; mapping class group orbits on covers

ideas.what: Category of oriented finite-type surfaces with isotopy classes of finite coverings as morphisms, described via (cover, marking) pairs
ideas.modern_name: Category of surfaces and finite covers up to isotopy (Teichmüller tower with covering morphisms)
ideas.usually_credited_to: implicit in work on Teichmüller tower / Hurwitz spaces; unsure of a specific credit
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the Teichmüller tower but mainly with gluing/degeneration operations

ideas.what: Profinite completion of Hom-sets via contracted product with \hat T_X; Hom^ is a compact profinite space with finitely many \hat T_X-orbits
ideas.modern_name: Profinite completion of a category with finite-stabilizer, finite-orbit Hom-sets

ideas.what: Composition of completed Hom-sets extending composition of covers
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure; related ideas in Mochizuki's combinatorial anabelian geometry and Boggi–Lochak's work on profinite mapping class groups

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a profinitely completed category whose objects are surfaces and whose morphisms are completed isotopy classes of finite covers, with composition (13), as a carrier for the Galois action. He leaves the composition and associativity explicitly unchecked.
missed.quote: (12) Hom^{\hat+}_isot(X,Y)=Hom^+_isot(X,Y) ∧ ... compactifié profini ... On définit une composition (13)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory mostly studies Galois or GT actions on individual \hat Γ_{g,n} compatible with gluing. Here the functoriality goes along finite covers between surfaces of different types (lifting of mapping classes, i.e. Birman–Hilden-type maps), assembled into a single category. Whether G_Q or \hat{GT} acts on this completed category is a natural, lightly explored question.

missed.claim: The completion is taken with respect to the full profinite topology of T_X. Making composition compatible with arithmetic actions ties directly to the congruence subgroup problem for mapping class groups. That problem is equivalent to asking whether the profinite completion agrees with the topology induced by finite covers of surfaces.
missed.quote: muni de la topologie d'espace compact ... compactifié profini
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This links the categorical construction to Boggi's and Asada's congruence-subgroup results. The topology defined by 'all finite covers X -> Y' is exactly the congruence topology, so this category is a natural framework for comparing the two.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains a concrete, previously unpublished construction: a profinite completion of the category of surfaces and finite covers, by contracted product with \hat T_X. This fits the Esquisse program but is not in published form, and it anticipates later categorical anabelian frameworks. The construction itself is sketchy and fairly natural, and is left unfinished.
transcription_corrections: In (12) and the margin, the group written as Γ_X in the transcription appears to be the Teichmüller group T_X (script T) and its profinite completion \hat T_X, consistent with the previous page. The formula reads Hom^{\hat+}_isot(X,Y) = Hom^+_isot(X,Y) ∧^{\hat T_X}_{T_X}.
In (13) the arguments are overwritten: Hom^_isot(X,Y) x Hom^_isot(Y,Z) -> Hom^_isot(X,Z), with Y and X corrected in place, and the label below reads 'notée'.

The right margin above (12) reads roughly 'muni de la topologie d'espace compact' with a bracketed, mostly unreadable remark ('[...] définition [...] Hom^ est [...]'). 'Topologie de convergence ponctuelle' is uncertain.
The insertion after 'combinatoires' reads '(i.e. de type f. et combinatoires)'. The crossed word before it is probably 'anciennes'/'orientées', uncertain.
